subject.title: [Feature]: SSRF 内网访问确认机制

question: Should OpenClaw add a browser private-network SSRF confirmation or allow/block policy, and which core policy shape should be approved first?
rationale: The request changes browser egress security semantics and public config/CLI surface, and current code has no existing approval or temporary-grant contract that automation can safely extend without maintainer intent.

options.title: Stage allow/block policy first
options.body: Approve explicit allow/block policy and non-overridable metadata behavior before deciding whether to add interactive approval UX.

options.title: Approve interactive confirmation
options.body: Commit to user approval prompts with timeout, rate-limit, audit, and redirect semantics across browser navigation paths.

options.title: Keep current model
options.body: Keep strict default plus explicit hostname/private-network opt-ins and document that broad LAN access remains an operator-controlled trusted-environment choice.

recommendation.title: Stage allow/block policy first
recommendation.body: Approve explicit allow/block policy and non-overridable metadata behavior before deciding whether to add interactive approval UX.

likelyOwner.reason: Recent merged browser SSRF/navigation hardening work touched the same guard and profile surfaces most likely to carry the design.
